segments.text: Goalkeeper Emi Martínez taken to hospital for 'precautionary' head injury tests. Sonay Kartal reaches Wuhan final as dream week continues. Loughnane, 20, becomes youngest champion jockey since 1923. Hello and good evening. I'm Kai Sprite, with Rosa Rally, and this is FULL TIME.
Hi, Kai. Hello, everyone.

Emi Martínez suffered a worrying-looking head injury during Chelsea's Premier League win over Everton on Saturday, according to ESPN. Chelsea coach Xabi Alonso told reporters that the Argentina international was conscious. Eleven minutes of injury time were added on by the officials at the end of the match following the lengthy stoppage in play. Two goals from Pedro Neto ensured Chelsea took all three points from their trip to Merseyside.
segments.headline: GK Martínez taken to hospital for 'precautionary' head injury tests

quote.text: I just said to TV, I've not seen the Martínez injury yet, so I hope he's fine. I really do. I couldn't even see from the dugout.

segments.headline: Today's results
segments.text: Let's go through the scores. Dundee United drew 1-1 with St Johnstone. Falkirk beat Hibs 2-1. Aberdeen beat St Mirren 3-1. Sheffield United beat Bristol City 1-0. Southampton drew 0-0 with Bolton. Elsewhere, Ulster beat Zebre 40-21.

Enzo Maresca has played down fears over Erling Haaland's fitness after the striker limped off at the end of Manchester City's 3-2 win over Ipswich. Haaland, who scored twice, looked in pain after a heavy challenge with Jack Clarke in stoppage time. "We will see," Maresca said afterward.
segments.headline: Maresca plays down Haaland injury fears

segments.text: Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom of the Scottish Premiership with a 3-2 victory over Motherwell. Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie's second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner, Sky Sports reports.
segments.headline: Kiltie double helps Kilmarnock beat fellow-strugglers Motherwell

standing.text: OFF THE BOTTOM OF THE SCOTTISH PREMIERSHIP

segments.text: How has their form been, Rosa?
Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann's side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point off bottom-placed Hibernian.

Portsmouth piled on the misery for struggling Norwich as they made it back-to-back Championships victories with a 1-0 triumph at Carrow Road. Pompey followed up their midweek win against Sheffield United with a hard-fought success in East Anglia, with a 51st-minute penalty from striker Marezi settling the issue. It was a fifth successive league defeat for the hosts and there were calls for sporting director Ben Knapper to go from frustrated supporters at the final whistle.
segments.headline: Struggling Norwich beaten by Portsmouth

segments.text: Alexander Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win as Brentford finish with nine, according to Guardian Sport. Andoni Iraola was delighted with how an attack worth close to £400m made the numerical advantage count after half-time. Isak’s Liverpool career has been stop-start since his £125m move from Newcastle, injuries holding the forward back.
segments.headline: Isak completes Liverpool’s comeback win

segments.text: Tens of thousands inside Etihad Stadium booed and jeered when the Premier League anthem was played over the speakers shortly before kick-off, then they started chanting 'City, City, City'. Manchester City fans boo the Premier League anthem before watching their side move six points clear at the top of the table. City fans arrived at the ground to find hundreds of inflatable bananas had been placed on seats in the home sections for fans to wave throughout the game. Here's Kai with the tennis.
segments.headline: Boos and bananas on day of defiance

quote.text: You can tell they are behind us and they're pushing us

segments.text: Britain's Sonay Kartal beats former French Open winner Jelena Ostapenko to reach the Wuhan Open final in only her third event after a six-month injury lay-off. The 24-year-old's composure helped her secure a 7-6 (11-9) 7-6 (7-5) victory in a pulsating semi-final against Latvia's Ostapenko, according to BBC Sport. "That was probably one of the toughest matches I've ever played," said Kartal.
segments.headline: Kartal reaches Wuhan final

segments.text: To the races now. Billy Loughnane becomes the youngest rider in over a century to be crowned Britain's champion jockey as he collects his trophy at Ascot. Aged 20, the Irishman beat five-time champion Oisin Murphy to the title, becoming its youngest holder since Charlie Elliott in 1923, according to BBC Sport. "I love my job and I love riding horses – it's all I ever wanted to do," said Loughnane, nicknamed 'Billy the Kid'.
segments.headline: Loughnane, 20, becomes youngest champion jockey

quote.text: I love my job and I love riding horses – it's all I ever wanted to do

segments.text: Ombudsman exacted Qatar Racing Champion Stakes revenge on Calandagan to come out on top at Ascot. When William Buick asked him to quicken, he scorched past eventual third Bay City Roller before seeing off Calandagan to banish Juddmonte International disappointment.
segments.headline: Ombudsman simply supreme in Champion Stakes

segments.text: Still to come: Jordan Henderson, the Premier League's oldest player, is becoming undroppable for Chelsea.

On to the rugby league. Brian McDermott says he can fix the errors that led to England's Rugby League World Cup defeat by Tonga. By the time Haumole Olakau'atu crashed over for Tonga's fourth try in their 30-12 victory, it was all over, BBC Sport reports. Due to the vagaries of the international rugby league calendar, this was McDermott's first match in charge of England since being appointed in April as Shaun Wane's successor.
segments.headline: McDermott seeks fix

quote.text: You cannot play with freedom at international level - you have to keep hold of the ball

segments.text: On to the basketball. Atlanta Dream coach Karl Smesko was optimistic that forward Allisha Gray would return from a finger injury to play in Game 1 of the WNBA Finals vs. the Valkyries. Gray led the team in scoring in the regular season at 19 points per game and is the best outside shooter for Atlanta with 3.1 3-pointers per game. The Valkyries have sold out every game at Chase Center during their two years of existence.
segments.headline: Dream's Gray expected to play

"We do understand how loud it is here and how supportive their fans are and what a great atmosphere and environment they've provided the W," Smesko said.

Time for the moment of the day. At 36 years old, Jordan Henderson is the Premier League's elder statesman. No sooner had referee Paul Tierney put the whistle to his lips than he found Jordan Henderson standing at his shoulder. Seconds later, Tierney amended his original decision and pointed to the corner flag.
segments.headline: Henderson is becoming undroppable for Chelsea
